The extension is Ø76 OD / Ø70 bore, so a Ø62.77 2×2 envelope would be 3.62 mm loose per side. Each spacer is a Ø66 clover with Ø26.5 pockets: 0.25 mm radial per cell,
The extension is Ø76 OD / Ø70 bore, so a Ø62.77 2×2 envelope would be 3.62 mm loose per side. Each spacer is a Ø66 clover with Ø26.5 pockets: 0.25 mm radial per cell,
1.37 mm wall at the corners. No per-cell wall is possible (cells on a 26 mm pitch touch) and no central collar is needed (four touching cells are mutually jammed — only the whole pack can slide).
1.37 mm wall at the corners. No per-cell wall is possible (cells on a 26 mm pitch touch) and no central collar is needed (four touching cells are mutually jammed — only the whole pack can slide).
Axially each spacer is SCREWED to its cap — that is what keeps the pack from sliding along the rod.
Axially each spacer is SCREWED to its cap — that is what keeps the pack from sliding along the rod.

clamping the disc — the cell springs push the disc OUTWARD onto its nut (compression). The rod's 10 mm of thread = 8 turns, 7 = 5.6 of them in the nut. 0.3 radial + 0.25 AXIAL flank clearance, off the

clamping the disc — the cell springs push the disc OUTWARD onto its nut (compression). The rod's 10 mm of thread = 8 turns, 7 = 5.6 of them in the nut. 0.3 radial + 0.25 AXIAL flank clearance, off the
rod's ridge: PETG threads without it lock solid. Plain shank in the middle, because a cell can come to rest against the rod (Ø10.77 void → 1.38 all round).
rod's ridge: PETG threads without it lock solid. Plain shank in the middle, because a cell can come to rest against the rod (Ø10.77 void → 1.38 all round).
Plastic, not aluminium: the rod is the only thing standing between four cans at four different potentials, and a conductive spine there is one nicked wrap away from a short.
Plastic, not aluminium: the rod is the only thing standing between four cans at four different potentials, and a conductive spine there is one nicked wrap away from a short.

Cell-to-cell insulation is each cell's own shrink wrap.

Shrink wrap is the standard insulation between cells in essentially every commercial pack. A user-replaceable cell does add ABRASION — it slides in and out against its neighbours and the spacer

pockets — so: a smooth pocket, 0.25 mm clearance rather than an interference fit (that is how you tear a wrap), and a re-wrap-if-nicked line in the manual.
